The 768 outcomes in collection-interface-reference.tsv are generated by the independent development-only C# recipes in ../reference/collection-interface.cs, executed directly on .NET Framework 4.0.30319.42000. Regenerate with Windows PowerShell and ../reference/generate-collection-interface.ps1. Neither the original Pascal compiler nor managed code is used by the native implementation or included in its portable package.

Six source families are tested: rank-one arrays, List, HashSet, Dictionary.Keys, Dictionary.Values and a user-defined ICollection<int>. The recipes cover all eight generic interface members and the inherited IEnumerator protocol, plus Enumerable.Count, default Contains, Contains with an explicitly null comparer, ToArray and Any. Each operation runs on a fresh empty or two-element source, including null receivers. CopyTo also varies null/empty/short/long destinations and negative/in-range/out-of-range offsets. Expected output includes the complete order of callbacks on the custom collection, not just returned values.

Fields are source kind, operation, size, null receiver, destination offset, destination length (-1 means null), output encoded as UTF-16 hex (- means empty), and native diagnostic code. Argument/range errors map to E_RANGE, null errors to E_NIL and unsupported writes to E_READONLY. The compiled native Pascal fixture executes the same operations independently; it does not call or translate the C# implementation.

LINQ callback routing here follows the existing legacy enumerable contract. A separate local probe against .NET 10.0.12 confirmed that newer Any uses ICollection.Count whereas Framework Any calls GetEnumerator; the native implementation preserves the legacy behavior. Invalid custom negative Count also differs for ToArray: the legacy buffer produces a null-reference error, whereas the newer runtime produces an overflow error. Runtime-version differences must not be silently substituted into this corpus.

Additional native checks cover Dictionary's ICollection<KeyValuePair<K,V>>, value-copy semantics for records, checked interface conversions and identity, generated sequences, readonly operations, List enumerator invalidation, rejection before output, and malformed collection type metadata. This is evidence for the implemented protocol, not completion of Collections, PABCSystem, ICollection on user records/ordinal range boxing or ICollection materialization/bulk insertion into List. Those remain explicit work. The later IList/indexed-property evidence is separate in list-interface-reference.md.
